CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with severe pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with severe left flank pain beginning three days ago. Pain is constant, radiating toward the groin, and patient is unable to find comfortable position. Hematuria noted this morning. Able to urinate despite pain. This is patient's third kidney stone episode; previous two resolved within 3-4 days. Has tried over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen without significant relief. Associated with chills, nausea, and anorexia. Denies fever.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, abdominal pain, or fever. Reports chills, nausea, and inability to eat.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, recurrent kidney stones (third episode), Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur.

MEDICATIONS
Amlodipine (Norvasc) 2.5 mg daily, Metformin 500 mg daily, Acetaminophen as needed, Ibuprofen as needed.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Difficulty adhering to low-sodium diet; prefers fried foods particularly french fries. Obtained blood pressure monitoring cuff but inconsistent with use.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated, attributed to acute pain. Heart: Regular rate and rhythm with Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (known finding). Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes. Abdomen: Tender to palpation without rebound or guarding. Flanks: Right costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness.

RESULTS
Fasting blood glucose in low 100s mg/dL (improved from 300 mg/dL two months ago). Hemoglobin A1C 7.3%. Home blood pressure: Systolic 130-150 mmHg, Diastolic 70-80 mmHg.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Recurrent kidney stone (third episode) with left flank pain and hematuria: Prescribe Oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours as needed for pain; continue acetaminophen for breakthrough pain; increase fluid intake; provide urine strainer; refer to Urology for evaluation and prevention of future episodes (referral to proceed regardless of spontaneous passage). Hypertension: Continue Amlodipine 2.5 mg daily; blood pressure adequate, no medication changes; reinforce 2,300 mg/day sodium restriction; continue home BP monitoring. Type 2 Diabetes: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily; current glucose control adequate; refer to Dietitian for dietary counseling on sodium restriction and glycemic optimization.
